newsitem.title: USA: Proffitt's sees 1997 Q4 EPS at $1.53.
newsitem.headline: Proffitt's sees 1997 Q4 EPS at $1.53.

text.p: Proffitt's Inc said Thursday it foresaw earnings per share for its 1997 fourth quarter to reach $1.53 before non-recurring items.
First Call's consensus among industry analysts projected a lower $1.17 a share for the same period.

The department store company also said it held an earnings target of $2.80 per fully diluted share for the year before such non-recurring items as a merger, restructuring, and integration charges primarily related to its acquisition of G.R. Herberger's.
First Call foresees $2.19 a share for the year.
"For the combined business, we remain comfortable with estimated revenues in the $2.38 billion to $2.43 billion range for 1997," the company said.
Proffitt's also said it expected 1997 first-quarter earnings at $0.39, $0.26 for the second and $0.61 for the third.
First Call foresees $0.31 a share for the first, $0.21 for the second and $0.44 for the third.

"This compares to 1996 fully diluted EPS (before non-recurring items and after restatement to include Herberger's) of $0.26 for the first quarter, $0.18 for the second, $0.49 for the third, and $1.14 for the fourth, for an annual EPS of $2.17," it said.
The company said it expected "certain non-recurring charges" in 1997 related to the Herberger's purchase ranging between $4.0 million and $5.0 million after tax, or $0.13 a share and $0.16.
In November, Proffitt's announced it was going to buy regional department store company Herberger's in a deal worth about $169 million.
